page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware configuration features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Cache resources comprise 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instructions including AVX-512, AMX matrix acceleration, and cryptographic acceleration extensions. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, representing an allocation of 16.0 GB per core. A 236 GB local NVMe SSD is bundled directly with the instance, and no discrete GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a significant performance divergence between single-core efficiency and parallel compute capacity. Single-threaded execution registers strong results, reaching 2160.0 in Geekbench single-core testing and 31.33 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics are limited by the two-thread total, yielding a multi-core stress-ng score of 1992.38 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2658.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 21.35 GB/sec, with write bandwidth measuring 14.43 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the server produces 2.83 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, 4.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 101.22 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M language model.

Regarding hardware utilization, the instance provides high qualitative efficiency for setups requiring large memory capacities and fast temporary NVMe storage without paying for unneeded vCPUs. This profile is advantageous for software licensed on a per-core basis. The primary tradeoff lies in compute concurrency, as intensive parallel processing will saturate the single physical core. The server is practical for in-memory caches, lightweight extract-transform-load tasks, and stateful application services requiring local scratch disk speed.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, creating a high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Its x86_64 architecture supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks show strong single-threaded performance, as indicated by top-quartile Geekbench single-core and gzip compression results. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are bounded by the low thread count, placing parallel processing and heavy database operations in lower benchmark percentiles. Without an integrated GPU, the instance functions effectively for in-memory caching, per-core licensed software, and memory-heavy workloads requiring fast local scratch disk access.
